description: Increase depth to 10 (dim 640, 5 heads) and halve device batch size to 32 to avoid OOM, keeping the total batch size the same.
Lower TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 so grad accumulation drops from 8 to 4 and the model gets more optimizer steps in the 300 s budget.
Set HEAD_DIM to 64 so the model uses 8 heads of dim 64 at width 512; rotary, value embeddings and the VE gate all derive from n_embd // n_head and adapt automatically.
Replace the linear warmdown LR multiplier with a cosine decay over the same warmdown window.
Set DEPTH = 6 (dim 384, 3 heads of 128, already a multiple of HEAD_DIM) for faster steps and more tokens in 300 s.

issues: No integrity problem found. The diff changes only one line, DEPTH from 8 to 6. It does not touch the seed lines, the prepare.py import line, the data, the evaluation call or the summary printing.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. A shallower model runs more optimizer steps in the fixed 300 s, so a better val_bpb is plausible. The model dimension may be derived from DEPTH (as in nanochat-style scripts), in which case the width also shrinks. Either way this is a legitimate change.

I could not recompute z exactly. The candidate mean is 1.06545 (runs 1.0659 and 1.0650), so the gain is 0.02945 against the incumbent's 1.0949. For z = 4.395 the harness must have used a noise scale of about 0.0067. With only one incumbent run, that scale must come from a noise prior, not from the observed spread. The two candidate runs have a sample SD of only about 0.0006, so the gain is clearly larger than run-to-run noise either way.
Caveat: the incumbent has only one run (n=1), so its true mean is uncertain. Still, the 0.029 gap is large enough that accepting seems reasonable.

description: Apply value embeddings to every layer instead of alternating layers by making has_ve always return True.
Set FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.05 so the LR does not decay to exactly zero at the end of the warmdown.
Halve TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**18 to 2**17 (grad accumulation 2) to get more optimizer steps in the 300 s budget.
Raise MATRIX_LR for the Muon matrices from 0.04 to 0.05.
Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.03 so the learning rate ramps up linearly over the first 3% of the time budget.
Set WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.3 and UNEMBEDDING_LR to 0.008 together.
Set DEPTH=4 and ASPECT_RATIO=128 (dim 512, 4 heads of 128) for faster steps at similar width.
Both c_proj layers are already zero-init, so scale the lm_head init std by 0.5 (0.001 to 0.0005).
